ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (, genjitsu).

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. It's like a big team of tiny experts working together, but they don't really know how they're communicating with each other, (kōryō).

The creators of these networks are like the team leaders, but they can't see the inner workings of the team, (kōryō). They can only see the results, like "oh, this is a good answer" or "this is a bad answer". They can't see how the team is making those decisions, (kōryō).

It's like trying to understand a really complex recipe, but you don't know what's in the sauce or how the ingredients are interacting, (kōryō). The creators can make the recipe work, but they don't really know how it's working, (kōryō).

So, even though these neural networks are really powerful, the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, (kōryō). It's a bit like trying to understand a magic trick, but you don't know how the magician is doing it, (kōryō).
